meta.title: Use of Laboratory Sink with Eye Wash in Pharmacognosy Laboratory

sections.purpose: To provide immediate first-aid decontamination of eyes and face following chemical splash or accidental exposure to plant saps, irritant latex, or chemical reagents in the Pharmacognosy laboratory.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmacognosy laboratory as an emergency first-aid station for ocular and facial decontamination, and for routine glassware washing operations.
procedure: For eye wash emergency use: do not delay — immediately guide the affected person to the eye wash station.
Activate the eye wash by pushing the handle forward or upward (plumbed eye wash) — water should flow automatically.
The affected person should hold their eyelids open with their fingers (overcome the reflex to close eyes) and position their eyes directly over the nozzles.
Allow clean water to flow continuously over both eyes simultaneously for a minimum of 15 minutes as per ANSI Z358.1.
Instruct the person to rotate their eyes up, down, and sideways during flushing to ensure complete washing of all eye surfaces.
After 15 minutes of flushing, have the person seek immediate medical evaluation — even if eyes appear clear, chemical injury may develop later.
For routine glassware washing: place dirty glassware in the sink; use laboratory detergent solution and a bottle brush for interior surfaces and a soft sponge for exterior.
Rinse with tap water three times, then final rinse with distilled water.
Invert washed glassware on the drying rack adjacent to the sink.
After each use, rinse the sink basin and eye wash nozzles with clean water.
Activate the plumbed eye wash briefly once a week (10–15 seconds) to flush stagnant water from the lines and verify function.
Log weekly activation checks in the safety equipment register.
precautions: Test the eye wash station weekly — stagnant water in the supply line becomes contaminated with bacteria and causes additional injury.
Keep the area around the sink and eye wash completely free of obstruction — the affected person must reach it within 10 seconds in an emergency.
Post clear signage (green cross / eye wash symbol) visible from all parts of the laboratory.
Train all laboratory staff in the location and operation of the eye wash during safety induction.
Do not use contact lenses when working with chemical reagents — lenses trap chemicals against the eye; remove before flushing if possible.
Do not use the emergency eye wash for routine glassware washing — contamination of the nozzle compromises its sterility.
For chemical burns involving HF acid, immediately flush then apply calcium gluconate gel — specialized protocol applies.
